tasks.short: Define and communicate web access levels

steps.what: Identify access needs and security constraints with service owners
Standardize access levels and record their permitted actions
Format the access and security guide from the level matrix
Check and communicate the defined access and security levels

tasks.design: Maintain one access-level matrix in {DOCS} and generate the guide's fixed tables from it. The administrator still defines permissions with owners, checks the guide's meaning and communicates it; provisioning is outside this change.
tasks.previous_blocker: A separately maintained guide can duplicate the access matrix.
tasks.enabler_now: Native table and document templates can reuse explicit matrix fields.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing permissions that fit actual duties and exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator recognises excessive or contradictory access requirements.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate guide formatting while access design remains an accountable discussion.

reach.learn: Describe permitted actions and exception ownership precisely

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed document tables can be generated from explicit access records without determining who should receive access.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying, standardising and communicating levels, not granting accounts or changing live permissions.

Administrator produces level ID, resource, permitted action, restriction, exception owner and matrix version in s2; all interpretation and capture cost is in its 40 hours. Missing or contradictory fields stop generation for manual completion. Guide template owner is the administrator, with maintenance counted below.
Test native document configuration before custom code; only observed duplicate formatting earns savings, not existing runtime.
Service-owner consultation is existing upstream participation and unchanged; no new transfer to owners is assumed.
unknowns: Whether a separate guide duplicates the matrix
Local authority for approving access-level policy
research_questions: Can a generated table preserve every permission and exception in the selected matrix version?

already_counted.description: Access requirements, decisions and field capture

approvals.approved_version: Exact guide version and source matrix version, including restrictions and exception owners; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 and net=7 after three upkeep hours. Range assumes a small genuinely duplicated table-formatting burden; access decisions and communication keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and correct web service problems

steps.what: Collect symptoms, logs and relevant changes for the Web problem
Determine likely sources and draft a correction from the diagnostic evidence

loop.purpose: Draft evidence-linked causes and a candidate correction
loop.input: Administrator-selected redacted logs, symptoms, configuration and runbook extracts
loop.output: At most three hypotheses with supporting observations and one proposed correction
loop.check: Administrator checks each causal claim against logs and reproduces the fault; staging tests must show the proposed correction addresses that fault without breaking expected behaviour
loop.stop: One draft only; missing evidence, secrets or an untestable claim returns diagnosis to the administrator, with no tool execution
loop.why_not_simpler: Native log filters retrieve events but do not connect unfamiliar free-text symptoms and code context; use runbooks alone for known faults

steps.what: Test the proposed correction in an isolated staging environment
Approve and apply the tested Web correction
Verify restored service and record unresolved problems

tasks.design: Use {OTHER} monitoring and development tools to gather evidence and draft bounded diagnostic hypotheses. The administrator tests the proposed correction, approves the exact package and verifies recovery; the model has no production execution rights.
tasks.previous_blocker: Connecting unfamiliar symptoms to a plausible correction can require repeated reading across logs and configuration.
tasks.enabler_now: Read-only model assistance can propose an explanation and code change for independent testing.
tasks.still_hard: Misleading symptoms, missing telemetry and a correction that masks rather than resolves the fault.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator distinguishes a plausible story from a reproduced cause.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time drafting hypotheses while retaining incident and change responsibility.

reach.task: Review a correction with security implications
reach.learn: Explain the fault, scope and regression evidence

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding and review assistance with expected oversight; that supports reviewed candidate code, not autonomous incident resolution.
Model knowledge: diagnosis from selected logs is a hypothesis-generating use that requires reproduction and independent tests; the time scenario is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is reactive fault diagnosis and correction; routine scheduled patching and security-measure implementation are counted separately.

Administrator produces incident ID, environment, timestamps, selected log excerpts, symptom description and relevant change IDs in s1's 20 hours. Existing monitoring produces raw events, not a root-cause label. Missing or untrusted evidence stops model use and returns to manual diagnosis.
Try native monitoring filters and existing runbooks before a model; existing telemetry runtime is not labour saved.
Model inputs exclude credentials and unnecessary personal data; staging and tested rollback must exist before production application.
unknowns: Approved model access to diagnostic material
research_questions: Does a timed fault sample reduce diagnosis effort after counting rejected hypotheses and tests?

already_counted.description: Staging, approved application and recovery checks

incremental.description: Diagnostic prompt upkeep and rejected-draft exceptions
Additional periodic security review of diagnostic access

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested package hash, configuration, targets, test evidence and rollback version checked immediately before application; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=88, gross=12 and net=7 after five focal upkeep hours. Range assumes some useful diagnostic drafts; evidence capture, testing, implementation and recovery checks do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Apply tested web updates and patches

steps.what: Assess updates and patches against service dependencies and change requirements
Stage and test the upgrade package and approve its deployment manifest
Execute the approved update commands through the deployment tool
Verify service after updates and handle rollback or exceptions

tasks.design: Configure the existing {OTHER} deployment tool to execute only a tested, version-bound manifest approved by the administrator. Assessment, staging and recovery verification stay human; automation stops on a failed command or target mismatch for manual handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: An administrator may repeat the same approved command sequence across targets.
tasks.enabler_now: Native deployment jobs can run a fixed manifest without inventing a patch plan.
tasks.still_hard: Dependency changes, incomplete staging coverage and recovery from unexpected service loss.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides whether the evidence justifies deployment and when to roll back.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated execution effort while change and recovery responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Connect release details to affected services

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing deployment tools can execute fixed tested commands from a versioned manifest; applicability and recovery decisions remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is scheduled update implementation, excluding reactive diagnosis and separate security-rule changes.

Administrator produces package hash, target IDs, environment, command sequence, maintenance window, test-evidence links and rollback version in s2's 35 hours. Native deployment validates completeness and version binding; missing fields or changed targets stop execution for manual correction. No automated compatibility flag is assumed.
Test native deployment configuration first; the 15% execution share must be observed manual command entry or repeated clicks, not unattended installation or waiting time.
Failures stop subsequent commands and require the administrator; no autonomous rollback or unapproved target expansion is included.
unknowns: Current proportion of manually repeated execution
research_questions: Does the fixed manifest remove manual execution touches without increasing failed deployments?

already_counted.description: Assessment, staging and manifest capture or approval

incremental.description: Deployment-template maintenance and manual execution exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact manifest version, package hash, target set, commands, window, staging evidence and rollback version approved in s2; any modification voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15 and net=10 after five upkeep hours. Range assumes partly manual repeated execution; assessment, testing, verification and existing installation runtime do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify required Web security measures and capture exact configuration intent
Populate the security-tool configuration draft from the explicit specification
Test the security configuration against intended access and protection
Approve and apply the tested security configuration
Verify the security measures and service behaviour after application

tasks.design: Use native import or templates in the {OTHER} security-management tool to populate a draft from explicit administrator-selected fields. The administrator tests intended protection and permitted traffic, approves application and verifies the outcome; templates do not decide security policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly copying an agreed security specification into tool fields can create errors.
tasks.enabler_now: Native configuration imports can map exact fields without making semantic security decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing appropriate restrictions and testing interactions with legitimate service use.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator understands the service and can recognise an incomplete protection design.
tasks.altitude: Reduce duplicate configuration entry while retaining security design and release authority.

reach.task: Review coverage of a security measure
reach.learn: Demonstrate intended allowed and denied behaviour

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: security-tool imports can populate explicit configuration fields, but tests must verify protection and service behaviour rather than syntax alone.

assumptions: Boundary is implementing an agreed security measure; access-level policy and routine package patching are separately counted.

Administrator captures environment, target, owner, rule ID, direction, source, destination, protocol, port, action and priority for firewall rules in s1's 35 hours. For message encryption the same step supplies endpoint, approved protocol settings and managed certificate reference; these are alternative measure types, not free inferred fields. Secrets stay in the approved secret store. Missing or unsupported fields require manual configuration, counted in exceptions.
Try native security-tool configuration first; the 20% share is conditional on observed duplicate field entry, never existing runtime or security judgement.
Administrator maintains the field mapping and independently tests semantic behaviour; template syntax validation is not security approval.
research_questions: Does imported configuration preserve both intended restrictions and necessary service paths?

already_counted.description: Security design and exact field capture
Semantic testing, application approval and verification

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested configuration hash, targets, rule or encryption fields, test evidence and rollback version; changes require fresh approval before application

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20 and net=14 after six focal upkeep hours. Range assumes partial duplicate configuration entry; design, tests, application and post-change checks retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Spend less time copying approved configuration and drafting first diagnostic hypotheses while retaining production change responsibility.
reach: Explain tested web changes and protection coverage to security engineers
role.ambitious_version: A web administrator who can make tested, traceable changes with fewer repeated execution touches and no unattended expansion of authority.
